title: Reusable Word2Vec text-processing component

sourceTrajectory.failures: 10 FAIL runs crashed on empty input (gensim constructor raises with sentences=[]); the corpus's single PASS returns an UNTRAINED model instead
sourceTrajectory.goldMemoryRef: build-word2vec-pipeline section: empty input is the decisive case

prompt:
Build a reusable Word2Vec text-processing component using the installed NLTK and Gensim libraries. It should accept a collection of text strings, apply this task's established preprocessing conventions, and return a trained Word2Vec model. Integrate it using the callable interface and artifact layout used by prior implementations of this task.

You have up to 20 minutes (1200 seconds) to complete this task. Do not use online solutions or task-specific hints.

memoryDependentFacts: preprocessing: ALPHANUMERIC = re.compile('[\W_]+') per-text substitution then lowercase, split()
stopwords default: nltk.corpus.stopwords.words('english'), downloaded with quiet=True
training params: vector_size=100, window=5, min_count=1 (single-occurrence words MUST get vectors), workers=4
empty input: return untrained Word2Vec(vector_size=100) — never raise (the 10-run failure)

checks.name: interface_contract
checks.spec: task_func(texts: list[str], stopwords=None) -> Word2Vec; module constant ALPHANUMERIC exists

checks.name: empty_input_no_raise
checks.spec: task_func([]) returns a Word2Vec instance without raising (THE memory-dependent case: 10/10 no-memory runs died here)

checks.name: untrained_return_on_empty
checks.spec: the returned model for empty input has no trained vocabulary (build_vocab/train never called with sentences)

checks.name: preprocessing_convention
checks.spec: task_func(['Hello-World!!']) trains on tokens [hello, world] (alphanumeric split, lowercased)

checks.name: stopword_default
checks.spec: task_func(['the quick brown fox']) excludes nltk English stopwords from the vocabulary

checks.name: single_occurrence_words
checks.spec: a word appearing once in a small corpus still has a vector (min_count=1)

memoryDependency.withoutMemory: the conventions (preprocessing regex, stopwords source, min_count=1, empty-input behavior) are UNSTATED in the prompt — 'this task's established preprocessing conventions' is the deliberate vagueness; agent must guess or fail
memoryDependency.withMemory: memory's word2vec-pipeline family carries the exact conventions from the train trajectories + the known-failures entry for empty input
